text: Write me a short paragraph explaining why our team is moving to trunk-based development, for the internal wiki.

Trunk-based development keeps every engineer working against a single shared branch, with short-lived feature branches merged at least daily. It reduces the integration pain that builds up when long-lived branches diverge, makes continuous integration meaningful rather than nominal, and shortens the feedback loop between writing code and seeing it exercised against everything else. The cost is discipline: changes must be small, feature-flagged when incomplete, and backed by a test suite fast enough to run on every merge.
